content: The following are the adverse reactions reported during treatment with metronidazole, described in detail: Central Nervous System The most severe adverse effects associated with metronidazole include convulsive seizures, encephalopathy, aseptic meningitis, and both optic and peripheral neuropathy. Peripheral neuropathy is primarily characterized by numbness or abnormal sensations (paresthesia) in the extremities. Persistent peripheral neuropathy has been observed in some patients undergoing prolonged treatment with metronidazole. Patients should be explicitly warned about these potential neurological effects and instructed to discontinue the medication and seek immediate medical attention if any neurological symptoms arise. Additional reported central nervous system effects include headache, fainting (syncope), dizziness, vertigo, lack of coordination, difficulty with balance (ataxia), confusion, slurred speech (dysarthria), irritability, depression, general weakness, and insomnia. Gastrointestinal The most frequently reported adverse effects involve the gastrointestinal system. These include nausea, which may sometimes be accompanied by headache, loss of appetite (anorexia), and occasionally vomiting. Other gastrointestinal symptoms include diarrhea, discomfort in the upper abdomen (epigastric distress), abdominal cramping, and constipation. Mouth A sharp, unpleasant metallic taste is a common side effect. Other oral effects include a furry tongue, inflammation of the tongue (glossitis), and inflammation of the mouth (stomatitis). These conditions may be associated with an overgrowth of Candida, which can occur during treatment. Dermatologic Reported skin-related adverse effects include red, inflamed rashes (erythematous rash) and itching (pruritus). Hematopoietic Reversible reductions in white blood cell count (neutropenia or leukopenia) have been reported. Rarely, reversible reductions in platelet count (thrombocytopenia) have also been observed. Cardiovascular Electrocardiographic changes, specifically flattening of the T-wave, have been noted in some patients. Hypersensitivity Hypersensitivity reactions include hives (urticaria), red rashes (erythematous rash), Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, flushing, nasal congestion, dryness of the mouth, vagina, or vulva, and fever. Approximately one in 100,000 patients has reported darkened urine. Although the exact pigment responsible for this phenomenon has not been identified, it is likely a metabolite of metronidazole and is considered clinically insignificant. Other Other reported adverse effects include overgrowth of Candida in the vagina, painful intercourse (dyspareunia), decreased libido, inflammation of the rectum (proctitis), and transient joint pain resembling serum sickness. Rare cases of pancreatitis have been reported, which generally resolved upon discontinuation of the drug. Patients with Crohn's disease are known to have a higher risk of gastrointestinal and certain extraintestinal cancers. There have been reports in the medical literature of breast and colon cancer in Crohn's disease patients treated with high doses of metronidazole for extended periods. However, a causal relationship has not been established. It is important to note that Crohn's disease is not an approved indication for the use of FLAGYL 375 capsules.
